props.title: Runaway Bride
props.initialSlug: A love story on the run.

sections.content: Runaway Bride (1999) reunited Julia Roberts and Richard Gere, attempting to recapture their Pretty Woman (1990) chemistry in a romantic comedy about commitment phobia. Director Garry Marshall crafts a small-town charm offensive, following newspaper columnist Ike Graham (Gere) as he investigates Maggie Carpenter (Roberts), notorious for leaving multiple grooms at the altar. The film taps into late 90s rom-com conventions while exploring deeper themes about self-discovery and authentic relationships. Like While You Were Sleeping (1995), it uses a close-knit community as both comic relief and emotional anchor. Pretty Woman|1990|A businessman falls for a sex worker in this modern Cinderella story|Netflix While You Were Sleeping|1995|A transit worker pretends to be engaged to a comatose man and falls for his brother|Disney+ Sweet Home Alabama|2002|A fashion designer must confront her past and first love before marrying her NYC fiancé|Disney+

The film sits at a crucial turning point in romantic comedy history. The mega-budget star vehicles of the 1990s were giving way to more grounded relationship stories. My Best Friend's Wedding (1997) had already subverted expectations by denying Roberts the typical happy ending. Runaway Bride plays it safer but still questions rom-com conventions about love and marriage, particularly through Maggie's journey of self-discovery - she doesn't even know how she likes her eggs because she always defaults to her current fiancé's preference.

The small-town setting follows a classic rom-com tradition established by films like Doc Hollywood (1991) and perfected in Groundhog Day (1993), where big-city cynics find unexpected romance and personal growth in close-knit communities. Marshall uses the quirky residents of Hale, Maryland, to both humanize Maggie and puncture Ike's urban arrogance, much like later films such as Sweet Home Alabama (2002). My Best Friend's Wedding|1997|A woman realizes she loves her best friend right before his wedding|Netflix Forces of Nature|1999|A groom-to-be questions his marriage during a chaotic journey with a free-spirited woman|Prime The Wedding Planner|2001|A successful wedding planner falls for the groom of her biggest client|Hulu SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Wedding-Themed Romantic Comedies

Runaway Bride kicked off a wave of wedding-focused romantic comedies that dominated the early 2000s. Films like The Wedding Planner (2001), 27 Dresses (2008), and Bride & Prejudice (2004) continued exploring marriage anxiety and identity through the lens of elaborate ceremonies. The film's emphasis on Maggie's career as a hardware store owner and her journey to self-actualization also anticipated later rom-coms like The Proposal (2009), where professional women struggle to balance success with authentic relationships.
